name: Poland
kernel_gaps: Rounding: Ordynacja podatkowa art. 63 half-up to whole zloty on grosze amounts (PlTax.Kernel.zl; kernel Rule.halfUp would fit, model predates it)
Schedule: written locally as PlTax.Kernel.Band/schedRaw before TaxKernel existed; bridged to TaxKernel.Schedule by KernelLink.bridge (all kernel Schedule/Unit theorems apply)
Social: employee contributions with a ceiling on two of three parts and a health contribution on wages less those contributions (contribution base depends on other contributions)
Social: self-employed contributions on a declared base independent of income, health by tax regime (9 % / 4.9 % with floor / flat revenue bands) - regime-dependent social rules
Credit: refundable credit capped by the taxpayer's own contributions (art. 27f ust. 9) with pooling between spouses (ust. 10) and an all-or-nothing income test for one child
Unit: per-business regime election (skala/liniowy/ryczalt) that disables splitting for both spouses (art. 6 ust. 8)
Exemption: revenue exemption with a shared cap (art. 21 ust. 44) and pro-rata apportionment of costs and contributions
Withholding: monthly advance engine (art. 32) for comparison with the annual tax

validation.notes: 48/48 mapped lines (CGTC, CGITLETC, CGITFP, SLT, EECSSC, CTGG) within 1 PLN; the 8 THP lines differ by exactly the employee half of the 7.3 % ZUS subkonto share, which the OECD leaves out as inheritable private-like savings (F1); OECD does not round to whole zloty (F2)

validation.notes: F13; no official PIT calculator found on podatki.gov.pl (the 'kalkulator taryfowy' is customs)

headline: Poland's 12/32 % scale with a 3 600 zl credit is exactly a 30 000 zl zero band (proved), and the OECD matches to the zloty once its subkonto convention is applied; the one-child relief limit (112 000 zl, frozen since 2013 and blind to ryczalt income) and the ryczalt health bands are notches with effective marginal rates above 100 %, while a sole trader on ryczalt at 500 000 zl pays half the tax and contributions of an employee.
